newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks up on election confidence, Dow Jones.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks up on election confidence, Dow Jones.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered from an uncertain start to advance in early trade on Tuesday.
Dealers said stocks that had lagged the recent furious rally led the market, fuelled by local and foreign buying amid positive market reaction to Sunday's mid-term elections.
"We're still climbing, brokers are confident after the elections and the Dow is also giving us a helping hand," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 28.11 points, or 0.58 percent, at 4,769.35.
Trading volume had picked up from a slow beginning to a moderate 10.7 million shares.
Mexico voted on Sunday to renew the entire lower chamber of Congress, one quarter of the Senate, several state governors and, for the first time in modern history, a mayor for the capital.
A preliminary count showed Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) with a 22-point lead in the historic Mexico City race.

The latest count also showed the Institutional Revolutionary Party was likely to lose control of the lower house for the first time since its founding in 1929. Final results are expected on Wednesday.
Spanish-Mexican financial group BBV-Probursa was up 9 centavos to 2.45 pesos in relatively brisk trade after lagging recent market gains, dealers said.
Financials in general were benefitting from forecast declines in domestic interest rates at the central bank auction later in the day, dealers said.
Dealers noted financial group Bancomer, one of Mexico's largest, had declined 3 centavos to 4.39 pesos after posting sharp gains on Monday.

Traders said help from the Dow Jones, up 28.50 points to 7,886.99, was most evident in market heavyweight Telfonos de Mxico (Telmex). The telecom's stock was up 20 centavos to a trading record in Mexico of 20.80 pesos.
Telmex ADRs were meanwhile up 5/8 to 52-1/2, their highest level since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
On the broad market, gainers outnumbered sliders by 42 to 13 of 70 stocks traded.
